sources.decision: Durability settings and explicit disposable-data exceptions.
Authentication rules are ordered; HBA snapshots do not prove TLS identity or actual matching.
Timeouts are workload/session scoped, not arbitrary global constants.
Autovacuum and maintenance require workload evidence.
Logical dumps are a supported backup mechanism; recovery objectives determine adequacy.
Backup/restore and maintenance concerns accepted; blanket claims that pg_dump is not a backup and VACUUM FULL is never valid rejected.
Pooling, replication lag and failover inspire contextual tests; no fixed pool size or universal partitioning rule.
Lock timing and overlapping application versions motivate migration/recovery tests; anecdote is not an admitted rule.
Expand/contract and representative migration testing accepted as contextual workflows. Claims that additive DDL is always safe or concurrent indexes take no locks are rejected.
Pool saturation/connection ownership inspires load cases. Fixed pool ratios and blanket prepared-statement incompatibility are not admitted.
Check pooler/protocol version, pooling mode, reset semantics and max_prepared_statements rather than universally disabling prepared statements.
Lock-chain diagnosis informs operator workflow. Example timeout values are not imported as universal global settings.
Concurrent index construction still has waits/constraints and cannot run inside a transaction block.

searchCoverage: Engine authors and specialist engineering blogs
